**Finding: missing (high severity) — no Customer termination for convenience.**

- **What I found:** Section 9 offers only for-cause (9.1), insolvency (9.2), and security/service-level (9.3) termination, plus a force-majeure exit (27.3). There is no Section 9.4 or any convenience right anywhere, while Section 8.1 sets a three-year term and Section 2.1 locks Customer into a USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay commitment "without reduction or termination rights." That is walk-away territory under T4C and fails the fallback (60–90 days' notice with a capped fee).
- **Direction check:** Vendor has no convenience right either, which suits us — so the redline does not disturb Section 9 beyond adding our exit, and simply confirms Vendor has no mid-term convenience right.
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** new Section 9.4 giving Customer a 30-day convenience termination with refund of prepaid Fees, plus a minimal carve-out in Section 2.1 so the new right is not swallowed by the take-or-pay lock-in. Fallback of 60 days' notice offered in the comment.
